Initially structured around two primary segments, Water Infrastructure and Applied Water, the company serves a diverse portfolio of public utilities, industrial facilities, agricultural operations, and residential or commercial property owners through a network spanning over 150 countries. By fiscal 2016, the business expanded to include a third segment, Sensus, which provides smart metering, networked communications, and data analytics for water, electric, and gas sectors, later evolving into Measurement & Control Solutions. This segment delivers smart meters, analytical instrumentation, and software services to optimize resource management and address challenges related to water scarcity, quality, and resilience. Throughout this evolution, Xylem maintains a substantial installed base that drives recurring revenue from aftermarket parts, maintenance, and repair services. The company differentiates itself through market-leading brands and a balanced sales channel combining direct forces with independent distributors. In fiscal 2023, the structure further adjusted to include Integrated Solutions and Services, which expanded to Water Solutions and Services by fiscal 2024, offering tailored services such as preventative maintenance, environmental remediation, and outsourced operations alongside equipment for industrial verticals like life sciences, microelectronics, and power generation. No single customer has ever accounted for more than 10% of consolidated revenues, ensuring a diversified client base ranging from government agencies and oil and gas companies to aquaculture operators and after-market buyers seeking support for equipment with lifecycles spanning decades.

CAPRI HOLDINGS LTD evolved from a global luxury lifestyle brand focused primarily on the Michael Kors portfolio into a diversified fashion luxury group encompassing Versace, Jimmy Choo, and Michael Kors. Initially operating through retail, wholesale, and licensing segments, the company sold accessories, footwear, and apparel via company-operated stores, concessions, e-commerce, and wholesale partners across North America, Europe, and Japan. Over time, the business expanded its licensed product lines to include watches, eyewear, jewelry, and fragrances through exclusive agreements with partners such as Fossil, Luxottica, and Estée Lauder, generating revenue through royalties and direct sales. By fiscal 2017, the group formally recognized Jimmy Choo as a distinct brand alongside Michael Kors, adding luxury shoes and accessories to its offerings, and later incorporated Versace into its three-reportable-segment structure. The company's product spectrum broadened to include ready-to-wear, haute couture, home furnishings, and wearable technology, distributed globally through a network of company-operated retail locations, wholesale doors, and licensing arrangements. While early years emphasized the Michael Kors luxury and accessible lines, later summaries highlight a strategic focus on expanding global footprints, particularly in Asia, and leveraging expertise in accessories and footwear to drive growth across all brands. The business maintained a diverse customer base ranging from high-end department store shoppers to mass-market consumers, with revenue streams increasingly driven by direct-to-consumer channels and wholesale partnerships while retaining ownership of trademarks and managing international distribution logistics.

TripAdvisor Inc. operates as a global online travel company providing a research platform that aggregates user-generated reviews and opinions on destinations, accommodations, restaurants, and activities, initially expanding from 18 media brands in 2011 to a portfolio of over 29 brands by 2012 and 34 countries by 2013. The business model relies on click-based and display-based advertising, subscription services, transaction commissions, and content licensing to serve customers ranging from individual travelers and online travel agencies to direct suppliers and destination marketing organizations. Over time, the company refined its operational structure, formally managing two reportable segments by 2016: Hotel and Non-Hotel, which later evolved into Hotels, Media & Platform and Experiences & Dining by 2019. By 2022, the organization reorganized into three distinct segments—Tripadvisor Core, Viator, and TheFork—where Viator functions as an online travel agency for tours and attractions, and TheFork operates a marketplace for restaurant reservations primarily in Europe and Australia. Revenue generation remains concentrated in these segments through advertising, commissions on facilitated bookings, and subscription tools, with the company acting as a merchant of record for service obligations while relying on third-party operators to fulfill specific travel needs. Throughout this evolution, TripAdvisor has maintained its role as a travel technology company connecting prospective travelers with global partners, leveraging proprietary ratings indexes and databases to facilitate transactions across approximately 7.5 million listed destinations while integrating mobile applications and social sharing tools to enhance its global reach.

CBRE Group Inc. operates as a global commercial real estate services and investment firm, evolving from a holding company with three geographic segments in 2001 to a structure with five primary reporting segments by 2004, which later consolidated into three main business segments by 2019. The company offers a comprehensive suite of services including brokerage for sales and leasing, investment property management, corporate services, commercial mortgage origination, valuation, and facilities management to a diverse client base comprising large corporations, institutional investors, pension funds, and government agencies. While revenue generation has historically relied on property management fees, brokerage commissions, and mortgage banking activities, the firm has increasingly emphasized recurring contract-based outsourcing services and account-based occupier solutions alongside cyclical transaction commissions. Its global footprint has expanded significantly, moving from operations concentrated in California and the United States to a presence in over 100 countries through more than 480 offices, with revenue sources shifting from approximately 75% domestic to a more balanced international mix. The firm differentiates itself through a full-service offering delivered under various brand names, including CBRE, CBRE Global Investors, and Trammell Crow Company, leveraging proprietary research and technology to provide strategic advice and execution assistance. Over time, the company has refined its operational model, introducing distinct segments for Global Workplace Solutions and Project Management to better serve occupiers requiring integrated facilities and program consultancy, while its Real Estate Investments segment manages capital for institutional investors across direct and indirect real estate assets.

WellCare Health Plans, Inc. operates exclusively as a managed care organization providing services through government-sponsored healthcare programs, specifically Medicaid, Medicare, and state initiatives like SCHIP and CHIP. From fiscal 2004 through 2018, the company sold health maintenance organization plans offering comprehensive medical benefits including primary care, preventative programs, hospitalization, prescription drug coverage, and enhanced services such as mental health and substance abuse management. Its primary customers were individuals eligible for these government benefits, encompassing recipients of Temporary Assistance to Needy Families, Supplemental Security Income, disabled persons, and Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 and over. WellCare delivered these services through extensive networks of physicians, specialists, hospitals, and pharmacies across numerous U.S. states, initially targeting individuals and communities rather than employer groups. The firm offered two main types of Medicaid managed care, including capitated plans where it assumed financial risk for state-specified services and primary care case management plans, alongside Medicare Advantage plans that provided fixed monthly payments in exchange for comprehensive hospital and medical benefits. Revenue was generated through fixed monthly premiums paid by government entities, covering healthcare services arranged for enrolled members, while the company competed for contracts, members, and providers in these public-sector markets without operating a commercial line of business. Over the years, membership numbers fluctuated based on CMS bidding outcomes and regional benchmarks, with the company managing member growth or attrition through network participation and benefit structures. The business model relied on contracting with providers to deliver medically necessary services while managing costs and quality in compliance with federal and state regulations, accepting financial risk for the management of beneficiary care.

Smurfit Westrock operates as a global leader in sustainable, paper-based packaging, producing containerboard, paperboard, kraft paper, and graphic board through vertically integrated mills and converting plants. Its primary offerings include corrugated containers, consumer packaging such as folding cartons, solidboard, bag-in-box systems, and paper sacks, alongside specialized services like graphic design, engineering, custom packaging machinery, and the manufacture of temporary and permanent display materials. The company serves a diverse clientele ranging from consumer and industrial product manufacturers to retailers, food service providers, healthcare entities, and the overnight courier sector. Sales are generally driven by customer orders for transportation and retail packaging, with a significant portion of converted product sales made under exclusive contracts. Operating across 40 countries in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America, the firm acts as a supplier to major brands like PepsiCo and Mondelez while also serving local businesses for national and regional clients. The business is organized into three geographic segments: North America, Europe/Middle East/Africa, and Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. In North America, the company utilizes an integrated system of mills and converting plants to serve primarily corrugated packaging, folding carton, food service, liquid packaging, and commercial print markets. The firm manufactures and distributes corrugated packaging, containerboard, consumer packaging including folding cartons, labels, and inserts, as well as bag-in-box solutions, while also providing contract packing services such as promotional packing and product manipulation. Sales are executed through a network of warehouses, distribution facilities, and specialized plants, with products tailored to customer specifications for transportation and retail display. The company delivers differentiated packaging solutions to the fast-moving consumer goods sector and diverse industries handling processed food, agricultural products, beverages, electronics, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals, utilizing a mix of direct sales forces and independent distributors to serve both pan-regional and multi-national accounts.

LyondellBasell Industries operates as a vertically integrated global chemical company producing olefins, polyolefins, aromatics, specialty products, and various ethylene derivatives alongside refined fuels. The company's structure evolved from five business segments in 2010 to six reportable segments by 2018, with the addition of Advanced Polymer Solutions, while maintaining core operations in Olefins and Polyolefins, Intermediates and Derivatives, Refining, and Technology. Production facilities are located across North America, Europe, East Asia, the Middle East, Australia, and Latin America, sourcing raw materials such as heavy liquids, natural gas liquids, and heavy crude oil to manufacture products like polyethylene, polypropylene, propylene oxide, styrene monomer, and oxyfuels. Customers span diverse industries including automotive, packaging, construction, industrial materials, and consumer goods, with sales conducted through a global network of direct sales offices, distributors, independent agents, and joint ventures. The company licenses polyolefin process technologies and catalysts under brands like Avant and Circulen, often utilizing multi-year contracts and spot sales to meet demand. Refining operations process crude oil into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, and distillates, selling these bulk products to other refiners, marketers, and wholesalers. Throughout the period, the firm expanded its reach into synthetic rubber, paints, coatings, and insulation sectors, managing domestic and export markets with a significant presence in the Americas, Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, while also developing recycled and renewable-based polymers in later years.

Allegion plc has consistently operated as a global provider of security products and solutions designed to keep people safe, secure, and productive across residential, commercial, institutional, and government facilities. The company manufactures and sells an extensive portfolio of mechanical and electronic items, including locks, locksets, door closers, exit devices, doors, door frames, electronic access control systems, time and attendance solutions, and various accessories such as bike lights. These offerings are marketed under strategic brands including Schlage, Von Duprin, LCN, CISA, Interflex, SimonsVoss, and Stanley Access Technologies. Throughout the period, Allegion served end-users across diverse sectors, specifically targeting education, healthcare, government, hospitality, office, and both single- and multi-family residential markets worldwide. The company's geographic footprint has evolved from three reporting segments covering the Americas, EMEIA, and Asia Pacific to a structure of two primary segments: Allegion Americas and Allegion International, serving regions including North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, and Africa. Sales are primarily facilitated through a vast network of wholesalers, specialty distributors, retail outlets, and e-commerce platforms, alongside direct sales to end-users through specific businesses like Interflex and Global Portable Security. While early summaries noted that the ten largest customers represented approximately 24% of total revenues in 2016, later filings confirmed that no single customer represented 10% or more of total net revenues in 2024. The company emphasizes a manufacturing strategy utilizing a global network of production facilities to ensure timely delivery, with security product sales often peaking during specific quarters due to construction and do-it-yourself projects in the Northern Hemisphere.

nVent Electric PLC designs, manufactures, markets, installs, and services high-performance electrical connection and protection solutions across a diverse customer base comprising panel builders, original equipment manufacturers, end-users, building owners, facility managers, energy contractors, electricians, telecommunications installers, and rooftop contractors. From fiscal 2018 through 2023, the company operated across three distinct segments: Enclosures, Thermal Management, and Electrical & Fastening Solutions. The Enclosures segment delivered innovative solutions for critical electronics, communication, control, and power equipment under brands such as Hoffman, Schroff, nVent Hoffman, and nVent Schroff. The Thermal Management segment provided electric thermal solutions, including heat tracing, temperature control, wiring, and freeze protection for buildings, infrastructure, and industrial processes under Raychem, Tracer, nVent Raychem, nVent Tracer, and nVent RAYCHEM and TRACER brands. The Electrical & Fastening Solutions segment supplied fastening, bonding, grounding, low-voltage power distribution, cable management, and tools under Caddy, Erico, nVent Caddy, nVent Erico, nVent CADDY, and nVent ERICO brands. These products connected and protected mission-critical equipment, buildings, and processes from hazardous conditions across industrial, commercial, residential, energy, and infrastructure verticals. In fiscal 2024 and 2025, the company reorganized into two primary segments: Systems Protection and Electrical Connections. The Systems Protection segment now provides protective enclosures, liquid and air cooling solutions, control buildings, switchgear systems, and power distribution for data centers and utilities under Hoffman, Schroff, TRACHTE, nVent HOFFMAN, nVent SCHROFF, and nVent TRACHTE. The Electrical Connections segment offers bus systems, cable management, and power connections under Caddy, Erico, ILSCO, nVent CADDY, nVent ERICO, and nVent ILSCO. These services are utilized by contractors, electrical utilities, electricians, panel builders, original equipment manufacturers, and hyperscalers to improve energy efficiency, ensure system resiliency, and enhance safety globally.

CSRA Inc. operates as a pure-play provider of information technology services exclusively to U.S. federal, state, and local agencies, organized into Defense and Intelligence and Civil segments. The company delivers tailored offerings including application development, IT infrastructure solutions, systems integration, and managed services across areas such as Digital Services, Enterprise Business Services, Digital Platforms, Cyber, Data Science, and Professional and Citizen Services. Key products encompass network and connectivity operations, software development and sustainment, data center management, cybersecurity support, and cloud-based applications. Major customers include the Department of Defense, specifically the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and various Joint Commands, alongside the Intelligence Community and federal agencies such as the Department of Homeland Security, Federal Aviation Administration, Environmental Protection Agency, Securities and Exchange Commission, Department of State, and National Institutes of Health. CSRA provides best-of-breed IT solutions, including open source and traditional platforms, to help government agencies derive value from big data through services like data science, visualization, and decision-making tools. The firm also operates Professional and Citizen Services, offering transaction processing, shared services, service desk support, workflow solutions, global visa processing, and organizational change management. These services enable clients to deliver efficient business processes and enhanced customer experiences using cutting-edge technology. The company's primary customers are U.S. federal government agencies, with a limited presence in state and local programs linked to federal work and projects in international markets sponsored by the U.S. government. The firm focuses on helping these agencies transition from legacy technologies to next-generation solutions in cloud, cybersecurity, and mobility while managing enterprise services with minimal resources. CSRA operates as a fully integrated company via its primary operating subsidiaries, CSRA LLC and SRA International, Inc. The company generates the vast majority of its revenue by acting as a prime contractor or subcontractor to other contractors under U.S. government contracts, often partnering with commercial technology vendors to provide hybrid cloud solutions and outcome-based services. The company provides a broad spectrum of services and offerings to the U.S. Department of Defense, including support for critical warfighter missions, and delivers mission information systems and technical support services to federal civil agencies such as the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of State, as well as to various U.S. federal, state, and local health departments. These services address missions including counterterrorism, environmental protection, and financial markets regulation.
